subject: Private offer: commit anchoring, list-price alignment and reseller buffer proposal
messages:
From: Emily Thompson <emily.thompson@scalehealth.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer: list price anchoring + reseller buffer for ScaleHealth

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers look great and the team is excited. Procurement looped me in to start the private offer conversation. A couple of specific asks from our side as we shape the PO: 

- We need the marketplace list price to remain visible/anchored for our internal catalog and purchasing team. Can you confirm the private offer can be set so the marketplace listing shows the anchored list price while the private-offer net to us reflects the committed discount?
- We work with a set of resellers and need a small reseller buffer (typically 8–12%) built into the private offer routing so partners can maintain margin. Is that supported by your channel/passback setup?
- Procurement would like to see an example pricing waterfall (list -> private offer -> reseller passback -> net Redwood rev). Can you attach a sample?

Timeline: We are aiming to execute a PO by the end of next quarter, but would like the pricing mechanics confirmed this month so our legal and marketplace teams can review. I attached our PO template for reference.

Could you confirm capabilities and provide a short proposed structure? If useful, happy to schedule a 30-minute sync.

Best,
Emily Thompson
Head of Procurement
ScaleHealth

Attachment: ScaleHealth_PO_Template.docx (docx, 52KB)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Private offer: list price anchoring + reseller buffer for ScaleHealth

Ben / Karthik — forwarding ScaleHealth's ask. Key points: they want marketplace list-price visible/anchored, a reseller buffer in the private offer routing (8–12%), and an example waterfall for procurement.

Quick thoughts / constraints:
- AWS/GCP private offers: we can publish a private-offer price while leaving the public listing unchanged; however, marketplaces often require the public list price to be >= private-offer per-region list-price constraints. We need to confirm region mapping with Marketplace Ops.
- Channel buffer: engineering supports routing that allows a fixed percent passback to resellers through our billing routing layer, but finance must approve the net % that Redwood recognizes.
- Recommended starting posture: propose a 10% reseller buffer with a 2% temporary cushion (12% effective) for the first 90 days, then step to 10% thereafter. That gives partners a small onboarding cushion while preserving our committed rev.

Ask: Ben — can you run a quick model (impact on net rev and tax) and tell me what the minimum net rate we can accept for a 12% buffer vs 10% steady-state is? Karthik — please confirm any marketplace listing constraints (AWS/GCP) we should call out in the customer note.

I can draft the customer-facing waterfall once you two sign off.

Thanks,
Dylan
Sr. Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Jun 2028 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private offer: list price anchoring + reseller buffer for ScaleHealth

Dylan — ran a quick pass in the attached workbook. High level:

- Base list price L = $100k (for example SKU set).
- Proposed private-offer discount to ScaleHealth: 15% (net to them = $85k).
- Reseller buffer: 10% standard (i.e., reseller gets $8.5k off the private-offer price), plus a 2% onboarding cushion for Q1 only (so 12% total in Q1). That results in Redwood recognized rev Q1 = $85k - $10.2k = $74.8k. After Q1, recognized rev = $85k - $8.5k = $76.5k.
- Implications: effective net rev delta between Q1 vs steady-state = $1.7k per $100k of list. Finance flagged that anything beyond 12% materially impacts target margin thresholds for smaller deals; recommend we cap buffer at 12% absolute.

Tax/comp: Note that reseller passback should be recorded as a contra-revenue line; confirm with accounting on resale flow if reseller invoices Redwoods or if Redwoods credits reseller via marketplace settlement. If the reseller is paid outside the marketplace, we need an explicit bookkeeping flow.

Attached: channel_margin_workbook.xlsx (model tabs: waterfall, regional-tax, timing-phases)

Ben
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
To: Emily Thompson <emily.thompson@scalehealth.com>, ScaleHealth Procurement <procurement@scalehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Jun 2028 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer: list price anchoring + reseller buffer for ScaleHealth

Emily — thanks for the clear ask and the PO template. Recapping and proposing a structure that aligns with ScaleHealth's needs and our internal guardrails.

Proposed mechanics (summary):
1) List-price anchoring: we will leave the public marketplace listing unchanged (list = L). The private offer will be published as a targeted off-list price for ScaleHealth; procurement can continue to see L on the public SKU page while the private-offer net is visible in the PO. Note: for AWS/GCP we will confirm region-level list-price parity with Marketplace Ops (see caveat below).

2) Pricing waterfall (example numbers):
- Public list (L): $100,000
- Private-offer committed discount: 15% -> customer net = $85,000
- Reseller buffer: 10% standard, with a one-time onboarding cushion of +2% for Q1 only -> reseller payout Q1 = 12% of $85k = $10,200
- Redwood recognized rev Q1 = $74,800; after Q1 = $76,500

3) Reseller routing and settlement: our billing routing supports a passback percentage that can be settled via marketplace settlements or via Redwood-issued credit to partners. We prefer marketplace settlement where possible to keep accounting clean; if partners require off-marketplace payments, we will include a contra-revenue treatment and document the flow.

4) Constraints and next steps:
- Marketplace Ops check: Karthik to confirm any per-region list-price constraints (especially on Azure/GCP where SKU mapping can create corner cases).
- Finance review: Ben to confirm final acceptable buffer cap (we recommend 12% maximum).
- Legal/PO: If this structure looks good, please return the PO template with a target signature window and I will send a private-offer draft (DocuSign link) and the channel-margin workbook for your procurement review.

Attachments: ScaleHealth_Redwood_PrivateOffer_v1.pdf (proposal summary), channel_margin_workbook.xlsx (detailed waterfall/model)

Proposed next step: 30-minute sync on Thursday 6/21 at 10am PT to walk the waterfall and settlement options. If that works, I will send a calendar invite.

Thanks — looking forward to progressing.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Sr. Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
E: dylan@redwood.com | M: (415) 555-0192
